entries.title: Insecurity and instability drive voters in Peru's tight presidential race
entries.snippet: After eight presidents in 10 years, many voters are looking for stability so the next president can focus on tackling crime and inequality.

entries.title: Funeral held for baby shot dead by Israeli troops in occupied West Bank

entries.title: Ragas and symphonies: Indian maestro Ilaiyaraaja is still reshaping music 50 years on
entries.snippet: Fifty years after his debut, Ilaiyaraaja remains one of the most celebrated composers in Indian cinema.

entries.title: 'It was either killed or be killed' - ongoing nightmares of an ex-child soldier in Somalia
entries.snippet: Yusuf Ali, now 34, struggles with his memories living in Mogadishu surrounded by dark reminders of his past.

entries.snippet: The US military strikes Iranian drones and radar sites and Tehran says it has targeted US bases in Kuwait and Bahrain.

entries.snippet: The Israeli military is investigating the incident in south Lebanon, where it is fighting Hezbollah.

entries.snippet: The Bulgarian singer says her historic victory in Vienna came close to never happening.

entries.title: Rumours and speculation as fans forecast date of Taylor Swift's wedding
entries.snippet: Swifties worldwide are looking for clues about the superstar's nuptials to American football star Travis Kelce.

entries.title: The cash-in-the-sofa saga that just won't go away for South Africa's president
entries.snippet: A committee of MPs has been formed to look at the case against Cyril Ramaphosa, but he may survive a vote.

entries.title: From Nescafe to Ted Lasso: Anthony Head's life in pictures
entries.snippet: Anthony Head, who first came to public attention for his role in 1980s Nescafe ads, has died at the age of 72.

entries.title: Giant banquets rile radical left in France
entries.snippet: The feasting phenomenon run by Le Canon Français has become a hot political issue.

entries.title: Fall in official Ebola numbers appears to be good news but it's not that simple
entries.snippet: There are now 380 confirmed cases of Ebola in DR Congo, far lower than initial estimates of suspected cases, writes Fergus Walsh.

entries.title: It's one of the world's most isolated islands. Here come the bulldozers
entries.snippet: The Indian government is spending $9 billion to create a megaport, airport and city on this remote island. Critics fear the impact on pristine forests and the lives of indigenous inhabitants.

entries.title: 1 million people flood Madrid streets to see the pope's flower-carpeted procession
entries.snippet: The crowd cheered and shouted "This is the youth of the pope!" as Pope Leo arrived for Mass at a central Madrid plaza. It's the first papal visit to Spain in 15 years.

entries.title: At least 12 people shot at an Ohio festival and a search for suspects is still ongoing, police say
entries.snippet: Gunfire erupted Saturday near a busy street festival in Ohio, wounding at least 12 people and sending some eventgoers scrambling for cover while others rushed to help the victims.

entries.title: 4 takeaways from the U.S. men's final tune-up games before the World Cup
entries.snippet: The U.S. men's national team chose to play a pair of highly-ranked, super competitive teams in the final lead-up to the World Cup: Senegal and Germany. The matches showed the U.S. is ready.

entries.title: When U.S. foreign aid changed, AIDS workers in Africa felt it
entries.snippet: In South Africa and Mozambique, health care providers say cancellation or redirection of U.S. PEPFAR funding under the Trump administration have already endangered vulnerable people and cost lives.

entries.title: Bumblebees have tiny brains but they can solve problems like chimps and elephants
entries.snippet: New research suggests the fuzzy insects may be capable of spontaneously solving problems the way animals with much larger brains do.

entries.title: SoFi Stadium workers vote to authorize strike ahead of World Cup
entries.snippet: Negotiations between the union representing the workers, the hospitality group at the Los Angeles stadium and FIFA are set to continue Monday.

entries.title: Why one historian uses social media to remember D-Day in real time
entries.snippet: At the National World War II Memorial, historian Alex Kershaw has found an unlikely way to keep D-Day alive: live social media posts timed to the events of June 6, 1944.

entries.title: Who will face Karen Bass? LA voters still waiting to find out
entries.snippet: Results are still coming in from the mayoral primary in Los Angeles. LAist reporter Frank Stoltze discusses who may emerge to face Karen Bass in November.

entries.title: Israel has reportedly used white phosphorus near Lebanese cities and towns. What is it?
entries.snippet: White phosphorus is not banned under international law, but can "create cruel injuries" and indiscriminate harm in civilian areas.

entries.title: Multiple people shot near festival in Toledo, Ohio, authorities say
entries.snippet: Multiple people were shot Saturday afternoon near a community street festival in Toledo, Ohio, police said.

entries.title: What to know about the protests and arrests outside a New Jersey detention center
entries.snippet: Clashes between demonstrators and law enforcement outside a New Jersey immigration detention center since late May have become the latest flashpoint for protests against President Donald Trump's immigration crackdown.

entries.title: What's next for the War Powers Resolution on Iran? PolitiFact explains
entries.snippet: The House and Senate have advanced war powers resolutions aimed at curbing President Donald Trump from continuing the war in Iran. Can a 53-year-old law make a difference? What steps would be required to end the war? PolitiFact explains.

entries.title: Former first lady of France Bernadette Chirac dies at 93
entries.snippet: Bernadette Chirac, the steel-willed former first lady of France who spent 12 years at the Élysée Palace from 1995 to 2007 beside President Jacques Chirac, has died at 93.

entries.title: U.S. mortgage rates are staying high – and the Federal Reserve can do little about it
entries.snippet: Investors' inflation expectations, much more than the central bank, are among the factors that affect the cost of home loans.

entries.title: Pope Leo XIV warns against 'fanning the flames of polarization' on first papal visit to Spain in 15 years
entries.snippet: Pope Leo XIV urged Spaniards on Saturday to stop "fanning the flames of polarization" as he arrived in Spain at a moment of political turmoil for the Socialist-led government and a credibility crisis for the Catholic Church.

entries.title: U.S.-Iran exchange of fire in Gulf tests fragile ceasefire
entries.snippet: Iran fired ballistic missiles and drones toward Bahrain and Kuwait that were intercepted early Saturday, Bahrain's government said, and called on Tehran to halt attacks on Gulf neighbors that test a fragile ceasefire in the Middle East conflict.

entries.title: Hegseth warns of 'invasion' and 'dangerous ideologies' in D-Day anniversary speech
entries.snippet: U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth used a D-Day anniversary speech on Saturday to appear to link immigration by sea to the wartime liberation of Europe, warning that the freedom won by Allied troops could prove temporary if leaders failed to defend it.

entries.title: Trump pardons former Republican congressman convicted of insider trading
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump has issued a pardon to Stephen Buyer, a former Republican congressman from Indiana who served nearly two years in prison for making illegal stock trades based on inside information after he left office.

entries.title: 7-month-old baby killed after Israeli troops open fire on a car, Palestinian health officials say
entries.snippet: Israeli troops shot at a car in the occupied West Bank, killing a 7-month-old Palestinian baby and wounding his parents, the Palestinian health ministry said, with the bullet striking the boy in the face.

entries.title: Trump says he wants Pulte to further slash staffing at national intelligence office
entries.snippet: President Donald Trump said Friday that he wants his new acting director of national intelligence, Bill Pulte, to cut the office, which has already been significantly scaled back during his second term.

entries.title: Why hiring surged in May despite economic strain from the Iran war
entries.snippet: There was surprising strength in the latest U.S. jobs report. Employers added 172,000 jobs in May, the third straight month of job gains. Overall, the labor market appears strong despite concerns about the Iran war, rising prices and artificial intelligence. Amna Nawaz speaks wit

entries.title: What may happen as oil supplies dwindle and Strait of Hormuz remains mostly closed
entries.snippet: As U.S.-Iran talks show little sign of progress, commercial traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains sharply reduced, raising concerns about global energy markets and supply chains. Geoff Bennett speaks with energy analyst Daniel Yergin, vice chairman of S&P Global, for more

entries.title: News Wrap: Senate passes $70 billion immigration enforcement bill
entries.snippet: In our news wrap Friday, Senate Republicans passed a $70 billion bill to fund immigration enforcement, Trump said he wants his new acting director of national intelligence to slash the agency's staffing, a federal judge struck down the Trump administration's immigration processin

entries.title: What Putin's rejection of Ukraine's call for talks means for efforts to end Russia's war
entries.snippet: Ukrainian President Zelenskyy is accusing Russia of choosing war over peace, after Russian President Putin rejected his request for an in-person meeting. Putin spoke at an annual economic forum in St. Petersburg, a city on edge after several Ukrainian airstrikes earlier this week

entries.title: Brooks and Capehart on some Republican lawmakers' defiance of Trump
entries.snippet: David Brooks of The Atlantic and Jonathan Capehart of MS NOW join Amna Nawaz to discuss the week in politics, including Republican defiance of President Donald Trump and fresh scandals in a key Senate race.

entries.title: Art exhibit shines light on women's role in technologies that power modern life
entries.snippet: Women have played a vital role in building the technologies that shape modern life, but their contributions have at times been overlooked, minimized or left out of the historical record. A new art exhibition seeks to tell a fuller story. Special correspondent Mike Cerre reports f

entries.title: This chef will teach you how to make healthy $5 family dinners
entries.snippet: With rising grocery prices, many Americans are struggling to provide healthy, complete meals for their families. One chef is teaching his TikTok followers how to eat well on a budget, one $5 meal at a time. Deema Zein reports.

entries.title: Energy Department says advanced nuclear reactor first to reach critical milestone
entries.snippet: The milestone occurs when a nuclear reactor achieves a self-sustaining chain reaction capable of producing a steady release of energy.

entries.title: As states face stricter Medicaid work requirements, Nebraska is an early test
entries.snippet: Millions are likely to lose coverage as states begin complying with the new federal rules.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Ukraine: Russian drone hits nuclear-fuel storage facility
entries.snippet: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has called a Russian attack on a nuclear storage facility near Chernobyl "vile." The UN's nuclear watchdog said no increased radiation had been registered at the site.

entries.title: Peru votes for new president — for ninth time in 10 years
entries.snippet: Peru could soon have its ninth president in 10 years, as voters choose between Keiko Fujimori and Roberto Sanchez in a runoff election overshadowed by instability and crime.

entries.title: Kosovo holds third election in 16 months
entries.snippet: Voters in Kosovo are heading to the polls in a snap vote called to resolve a parliamentary stalemate. The country's prolonged political crisis has further debilitated an already ailing economy.

entries.title: Germany news: Far-right AfD makes push in district elections
entries.snippet: Sunday's district polls are seen as a barometer for elections in eastern states in September. Meanwhile, Chancellor Merz is headed to London to discuss the Ukraine war as Putin rejects face-to-face talks. DW has more.

entries.title: Israel's military says it struck southern Beirut days after a shaky ceasefire with Lebanon was announced
entries.snippet: The Israeli military said it is carrying out strikes on infrastructure it says belongs to Iran-backed Islamist group Hezbollah. This comes after it said projectiles were shot at Israel earlier today. DW has more.

entries.title: India news: CJP demands minister's removal in seven days
entries.snippet: The Cockroach Janta Party has given an ultimatum for the removal of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Meanwhile, the Indonesian foreign minister is visiting Delhi. Follow DW for more.

entries.title: Armenia, once Russia's reliable ally, considers an EU future
entries.snippet: Armenians are set to vote on the country's future geopolitical direction on June 7. The election will be a test of public opinion in the long-standing Russia ally, where the population is increasingly eyeing the EU.

entries.title: Taiwan deploys vessels in response to Chinese operation
entries.snippet: Taiwan's coast guard confronts Chinese vessels near the island after Beijing launched what it called a "law enforcement operation."

entries.title: Ethiopia's election results will likely confirm status quo
entries.snippet: Ethiopia's ruling Prosperity Party is set for a decisive election win when results are announced. The election was marked by security challenges, a divided opposition and the exclusion of entire regions from voting.

entries.title: Armenia goes to polls, with Russia and EU looking on
entries.snippet: Armenians are voting in elections that pit pro-EU Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan against the pro-Russia opposition. Peace efforts with longtime foe Azerbaijan are also a main election issue.

entries.title: US: 12 injured after shooting near festival in Ohio, police hunt suspects
entries.snippet: Authorities said two of the victims are in critical condition after a gunfire near Toledo's Old West End Festival, with suspects still on the run.

entries.title: North Korea says nuclear program 'absolutely nonnegotiable'
entries.snippet: Kim Yo Jong, the sister of North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, has reaffirmed the country's nuclear ambitions ahead of a visit by Chinese President Xi Jinping.

entries.title: Germany beat USA before World Cup but injuries cast shadow
entries.snippet: Germany’s final match before their World Cup start ended with a 2-1 win. But a tournament-ending injury to rising star Lennart Karl and doubts about veteran Manuel Neuer mean coach Julian Nagelsmann has work to do.

entries.title: UK: 6 more charged after violent protest over stabbing death
entries.snippet: A total of 11 people have been charged with violent disorder following the stabbing of a student. UK Prime Minister Starmer has criticized right-wing politicians such as the US vice president for exploiting the case.

entries.title: Ukraine hits St. Petersburg again after Putin rejects talks
entries.snippet: Ukrainian drones targeted St. Petersburg and the surrounding region for a second time after Russian President Vladimir Putin rejected Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's offer of peace talks.

entries.title: French Open: Andreeva wins first Grand Slam tennis title
entries.snippet: Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva beat Polish qualifier Maja Chwalinska in the final in Paris. She is the first Russian woman to win a Grand Slam since Maria Sharapova won the French Open in 2014.

entries.title: High-functioning depression: When success masks suffering
entries.snippet: People with depression don't always feel overwhelmed or struggle to get things done — some are highly efficient and productive, despite their low moods. So it can't be that bad, right? Wrong!

entries.title: Hunger in Oleshky: Ukraine asks for evacuation
entries.snippet: The Ukrainian city of Oleshky has been occupied by Russian troops since 2022. Many residents are cut off from the outside world and living in dire conditions. Now, Kyiv wants to rescue them.

entries.title: France: Veterans mark 82nd anniversary of D-Day in Normandy
entries.snippet: The last living World War II veterans have made the journey to France to commemorate the Normandy landings, which mark the beginning of the Allied campaign to liberate Western Europe from Nazi Germany.
